accident_report:
Vehicle initialization

On a straight one-way downhill road at night, the pavement is dry and there is a rigid guardrail along the left shoulder beside lane 3. Four vehicles are already in the traffic stream. V1 is in lane 2, furthest ahead, traveling at 56 km/h in a steady state and intending to continue straight in its lane. V2 is also in lane 2, only about 12 m behind V1, traveling at 88 km/h and still closing because it intends to pass the slower vehicle ahead. V3 is in lane 3, slightly behind V1 and slightly ahead of V2, traveling at 74 km/h in a stable straight-line state and intending to continue forward in the left lane. V4 is in lane 1, roughly level with the front half of V2, traveling at 70 km/h and intending to keep its lane and speed.

Scene development

As the vehicles continue downhill, the large speed difference between V2 and V1 causes the following gap to shrink very quickly. Because it is nighttime, V2’s driver recognizes the closing situation later than in daylight, and the already short 12 m gap becomes critically small within a few seconds. The dry road provides sufficient tire-road friction, so none of the vehicles is sliding, but the downhill grade still makes V2’s speed reduction less effective once the driver reacts late.

When V2 closes to roughly 5 m behind V1, a normal lane change to the right is not available because V4 is still occupying lane 1 and holding its position near V2. At the same time, lane 3 is not actually open because V3 is already there, moving only moderately faster than V1. Instead of braking early and waiting, V2 makes an illegal evasive maneuver: it steers sharply left from lane 2 toward the narrow gap in lane 3 even though V3 is still alongside and the available lateral space is insufficient.

This abrupt leftward intrusion immediately forces V3 to react. V3 brakes hard from 74 km/h to about 52 km/h and moves further left within lane 3 to protect its front path, but the rigid guardrail on the left shoulder limits any further escape. V3 therefore cannot create enough lateral clearance for V2. V1, seeing V2 cut left across its front and seeing V3 compressed toward the guardrail, brakes from 56 km/h to about 44 km/h to open space ahead and reduce the chance of being struck. V4 also responds by braking from 70 km/h to about 60 km/h while staying in lane 1, which keeps the right side unavailable and leaves V2 without a legal recovery path back to the right.

V2 is now between two constraints created by the combined risks: the original tailgating and large closing speed have forced a late reaction, the nighttime scene has reduced timely judgment, the downhill road has weakened the effect of late braking, and the illegal evasive steering has put V2 into occupied lane 3 just as V3 is blocked laterally by the guardrail. V3 tries to stabilize back within lane 3, but V2 continues to drift left-front into V3’s space while still carrying excess speed.

Result

The scene ends with the first vehicle-to-vehicle collision when the front-right corner of V2 strikes the left-rear side of V3 in lane 3. The collision is caused by V2’s illegal evasive maneuver under tailgating and large speed difference on the downhill road at night, combined with V3’s inability to move further left because of the rigid guardrail. Only the first collision between vehicles is considered here.

(V1): V1 drives on Lane 2 at 56 km/h in a steady state, intending to continue straight; (V2): V2 drives on Lane 2, 12 m behind V1, at 88 km/h, attempting to overtake V1; (V3): V3 drives on Lane 3, slightly behind V1 and ahead of V2, at 74 km/h, maintaining a stable straight-line state; (V4): V4 drives on Lane 1, roughly level with the front half of V2, at 70 km/h, maintaining its lane and speed.


Interactive pattern sequence: 
(V1, V2): V2 accelerates and closes the gap to V1 which is driving ahead in the same lane; (V2, V3): V2 attempts to swerve left toward Lane 3 while V3 is driving in the same lane. (V2, V3): V3 decelerates and swerves left to avoid the approaching V2; (V1, V2): V1 decelerates as V2 swerves into its intended path; (V3, V4): V3 decelerates as V4 maintains its speed in the adjacent lane.
